newsitem.title: USA: Clark Gable's Oscar fetches record $550,000.
newsitem.headline: Clark Gable's Oscar fetches record $550,000.

text.p: The Oscar that Clark Gable won for his role in the 1934 film "It Happened One Night" was auctioned off on Sunday for a record $550,000.
Officials with Christie's auction house said the 12-inch (30 cm) gold-plated Oscar statuette was sold to an unidentified telephone bidder within minutes of being put on the block.

The winning bid topped the previous record price for an Oscar of $510,000, set in 1993 at Sotheby's auction house for the statuette given to Vivien Leigh when she won the best actress Academy Award for her role opposite Gable in "Gone With the Wind."
Officials with Christie's attributed Sunday's record bid to Gable's popularity as one of Hollywood's most famous stars.
"He is still the leading man for many people," said Vredy Lytsman, a spokeswoman for Christie's in Los Angeles.

Gable won the Oscar for his role as a wise-cracking newspaper reporter in love with a runaway heiress, played by Claudette Colbert. The film swept the Academy Awards, taking best film honours and garnering Oscars for Colbert and director Frank Capra in addition to Gable.

The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, which hands out the Academy Awards every year, tried unsuccessfully on Friday to block the sale, saying the Oscar statuettes were never intended to be articles of trade.
